liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **The Stranger (Two Souls In Communion)** (1 review, 1 other source): Pigpen's performance is called classic Pigpen, with the band knowing the changes; Described as a very rare Pigpen composition, played only 13 times [17][24]
- **Next Time You See Me** (1 review): Next Time You See Me and other blues numbers have a honky-tonk, barroom band feel, with Pigpen in strong form [15]
- **Truckin'** (1 review): Top-drawer Truckin' leads into a roughly 17-minute Other One, which eases into a fine Wharf Rat [8]
- **The Other One** (1 review): Reviewer describes soaring versions of The Other One going into Wharf Rat [10]
- **Big Railroad Blues** (1 review): Called the standout tune of the night and one of the best versions ever [12]
- **Two Souls In Communion** (1 review): Pigpen is singled out in Two Souls; the tape is cut off at the second set's high point [11]

## Setlist highlights

- Earliest performances in the archive: Looks Like Rain, The Stranger (Two Souls In Communion) [18]

## The recordings

- **gd1972-03-21.sbd.miller.92395.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 28 songs; 210 min; rated 4.48/5 by 21 [1]. Said about its sound: Initial mixing problems and a hum are noted at the start of the recording; A bad hum from a grounding issue eventually gets fixed; many flaws removed but some remain [1][15]
- **gd1972-03-21.136670.sbd.sirmick.flac16**: soundboard; 27 songs; 199 min; rated 5/5 by 3 [2]. Said about its sound: Uploader says this source has relatively few problems compared with the Miller version [2]
- **gd72-03-21.sbd.vernon.9331.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 13 songs; 87 min; rated 4/5 by 5 [3]. Said about its sound: Audio is not great, with some raspy spots in the recording; Reviewer says this recording sounds great [6][10]
- **gd1972-03-21.set2-sbd.Samaritano.32370.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 12 songs; 86 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [4]. Said about its sound: Reviewer praises the soundboard's mix, recording and transfer as top quality [17]
- **gd72-03-21.sbd-disk1.samaritano.15041.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 9 songs; 72 min; rated 4.83/5 by 6 [5]. Said about its sound: Near-perfect clear sound with minor pops; the recording is only a partial show; Reviewer rates the sound quality top marks; the recording is a strong partial set; Reviewer calls the recording crisp [8][9][12]

## Around the show

- Reviewer says New York crowds loved Pigpen and brought out the best in the band [17]
- The recording has a cut during the intro to Chinatown Shuffle [1]
- Reviewer treats the show as a warm-up for the Europe 1972 tour [12]
- Reviewer calls it a dress rehearsal for the Europe Tour, building on groundwork laid in autumn 1971 [15]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1972-03-21.sbd.miller.92395.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Unknown; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel [1]. Also: Source comes from DATs lent by Rob Eaton; disc changes are seamless with tuning tracks added [1]
- **gd1972-03-21.136670.sbd.sirmick.flac16**: taped by Anonomous; transferred by SIRMick; source: Source: sbd > cassette master > dat(48k) [2]. Also: This version came from an anonymous source [2]
- **gd72-03-21.sbd.vernon.9331.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [3]
- **gd1972-03-21.set2-sbd.Samaritano.32370.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Joe Samaritano; source: MSR>Dat>Dat>Sonic Solutions>CD [4]
- **gd72-03-21.sbd-disk1.samaritano.15041.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [5]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by johnsdeadart.blogspot.com: [John's Custom Grateful Dead Album Cover Art](https://johnsdeadart.blogspot.com/2017/05/blog-post_90.html) [20]
- Fan art by johnsdeadart.blogspot.com: [John's Custom Grateful Dead Album Cover Art](https://johnsdeadart.blogspot.com/2017/05/blog-post_90.html) [21]
